summary: Piscataquis County, ME: lookout site first used in 1913; tower still stands with its cab gone; state plan calls it closed; the road to the trailhead is private but publicly accessible, and trail access is not guaranteed.

facts.design: Tower described as 48 feet in a May 1935 newspaper item; the cab is no longer in place
facts.status_note: The tower still stands, but its cab is gone (FFLA).

access.note: The 2014 Bureau of Parks and Lands plan calls the tower closed; do not climb it. The trail starts from Meadow Brook Road, which is privately owned but publicly accessible, and access is not guaranteed.

visit.trail_note: About 1.7 miles one way on a primitive footpath from the trailhead (Maine Trail Finder)

notes_for_editor: The FFLA list and legend give the current standing (structure kept, cab gone). The state plan says closed and the Maine by Foot guide says a climbable ladder remains; we follow the plan and do not encourage climbing, and the disagreement is stated in the story. The 1935 48-foot height may not describe the present structure, so no height_m is recorded. The 2014 plan calls the trailhead to be developed while the Pinnacle page gives directions to a temporary parking area and is undated, so the current trailhead is unconfirmed. The Forest Lookouts page gives the agency as the Maine Forestry District only. Ownership of the tower site was not confirmed. No corrections proposed to the record.
